- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and underperform when sentiment is low (<0.4), especially near 0.0.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high or 10% below recent 30d mean.
- Underestimate during prolonged low sentiment (e.g., 0.0–0.2) — adjust downward by 2–5% of recent 10d range.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30d mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops sharply 2–3 days prior, reduce forecast by 3–5% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — use 14d rolling mean as anchor for correction.
